title: Predictive GPU Headroom Sensor and Simulation Harness for Weight/KV/Activation Budgeting
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Build a telemetry-driven 'headroom sensor' plus an offline simulation harness to produce per-GPU safe headroom budgets that account for weights, KV cache growth, and activation peaks. This feature aims to reduce conservative static reservations that waste capacity while preventing OOM/evictions during bursty traffic.

Background: We currently reserve a fixed margin per GPU to protect against KV/activation growth and rare long-sequence requests. That margin is conservative and causes underutilized capacity on Dedicated pools and higher unit costs for Hosted. Ad-hoc manual adjustments lack telemetry fidelity and do not cover cross-tenant variance.

Goals:
- Produce a per-GPU dynamic headroom recommendation (in MB) that covers the 99th percentile of observed memory demand over a configurable window.
- Expose the recommendation as a realtime sensor (Kafka topic + Console metric) and as an offline Monte Carlo simulation report for rollout planning.
- Integrate the sensor with the scheduler to enable preemptive admission control and graceful fallback when headroom is predicted to be insufficient.

Approach:
1) Telemetry dataset: collect time-series features per-GPU per-epoch: active_model_variant_size_bytes, kv_bytes_used, kv_prefix_hit_rate, concurrent_streams, avg_sequence_length, batch_size_distribution, shader/activation_bytes, temperature (hardware), and recent eviction_count. Store samples at 10s cadence in the new headroom-metrics topic.
2) Modeling: build a lightweight ensemble (histogram-augmented quantile regressor) that predicts the 95/99 memory demand percentile given current features and short-term trend features (delta over 60s/5min). Keep model small so it can run in the control plane without GPU.
3) Simulation harness: offline Monte Carlo runner that replays historical traffic mixes and synthetic spike scenarios to compute recommended safety multipliers and estimate cost savings vs. current static margin. The harness will output per-cluster reports, eviction-risk curves, and suggested rollout thresholds.
4) Integration: publish sensor to Kafka and Grafana, wire an alert when predicted headroom < configured safety threshold; expose API for scheduler to query per-GPU headroom and to trigger admission control.

Acceptance criteria:
- Sensor is producing predictions for >=90% of GPUs in staging with latency <500ms.
- Simulation harness can run a 7-day replay in <2h for a 200-GPU fleet snapshot and produce eviction-risk curves.
- In canary, dynamic headroom reduces aggregate reserved memory by >=10% without increasing eviction incidents over baseline for the canary window.
- Console shows headroom time-series, and there is an actionable alert and runbook when predicted headroom falls below threshold.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Model complexity vs execution cost: we prefer a small quantile regressor to a large neural net to avoid compute on the control plane and to keep explainability.
- Conservative tail coverage: we target 99th percentile by default but allow operator override to 95/99.9 per deployment.
- Reaction speed vs stability: smoothing windows balance responsiveness to bursts and avoiding churn in allocation decisions; default smoothing is 30s for short-term detection and 5m for trend.

Open questions / risks:
- Telemetry completeness for on-prem/private deployments where we cannot push metrics to the control plane. Proposed mitigation: run local headroom agent that emits sensor via customer-managed Kafka or exposes it via the local control mesh.
- Interaction with quantized weight variants (different weight sizes): need mapping layer so predictions account for pinned model variant.

Artifacts:
- Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-26188+GPU+Headroom+Sensor
- Simulation harness repo (prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/headroom-sim/tree/eng-26188
- Notebook with sample replays and plots: https://github.com/redwood-inference/headroom-sim/blob/eng-26188/notebooks/replay-analysis.ipynb
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/Headroom/headroom-sensor-overview
- Initial performance dashboard (staging): https://telemetry.redwood.ai/d/runtimes/headroom-canary

Rollout plan:
- Week 1 (staging): telemetry instrumentation and lightweight predictor in control plane (read-only). Run simulation for last 30d and generate reports.
- Week 2 (canary): enable sensor-driven admission control for <=10% of Dedicated pools, monitor evictions and latency.
- Week 3 (expand): increase canary to 50% after verification, add Console controls for operator thresholds.
- Week 4 (GA): enable default for new capacity pools and provide rollout docs for existing customers.

Runbook (short):
- If predicted headroom drops below threshold and evictions increase: 1) trigger automated throttle for bursty queues 2) temporarily increase reservation multiplier for affected GPUs 3) investigate request patterns via headroom-metrics dashboard 4) open incident with infra on-call if unresolved after 15m.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Kickoff meeting notes: scoped telemetry schema and agreed 10s cadence. Action: Liam to add metrics to agent SDK and Asha to prototype simulator dataset ingestion.

2026-02-17 - Prototype model trained on 30 days of staging telemetry; initial quantile regressor achieves ~6% MAE on 95th percentile targets. Preliminary sim shows possible 12% reserved-memory reduction for low-variance workloads.

2026-02-22 - Review feedback from Sofia Martinez: add guard rails for private deployments and require opt-in for GA. Also requested exportable CSV report for compliance teams. Action: Liam to add CSV export to harness.

2026-02-26 - Found a corner case where long-running streaming sessions steadily grow KV by 20MB/min causing slow leak risk. Mitigation: add leak-detection feature that trips when kv_bytes_used growth rate sustained > configured slope for 10m.
2026-03-01 - PR opened for control-plane predictor and metric export: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/5423. Requesting review from @sofia and @marc.

2026-03-03 - Load test results: canary scheduler accepted 18% more short requests before needing to throttle, with no evictions during 4h run. Latency 95th increased by 2.1% in worst bucket. QA flagged a flaky metric emission in older agents; fix deployed to staging agents v0.9.7.
2026-03-05 - Design review approved by infra leads. Next steps: finish on-prem agent flow, finalize runbook, and schedule canary deployment for 2026-03-09.
